entry.title: I built a free cron expression decoder, here's how it works under the hood
entry.summary:
The problem
Every developer has been here: you're staring at 0 */4 * * 1-5 in a config file I got tired of that. So I built Cron.Explain, a free tool that decodes any cron expression into plain English instantly. 🔗 https://timely-flan-0ca3c1.netlify.app Paste any cron expression and you get three things: 1. Plain English explanation 0 9 * * 1-5 → "At 9:00 AM, on Monday through Friday" 2. Field-by-field breakdown 3. Next 5 run times It also ships a free REST API — no key required: curl -X POST https://timely-flan-0ca3c1.netlify.app/api/explain \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"cron": "0 9 * * 1-5"}'
Response: { "expression": "0 9 * * 1-5", "explanation": "At 9:00 AM, on Monday through Friday", "fields": { ... }, "nextRuns": ["2026-02-23T09:00:00.000Z", ...] }
The interesting part: I didn't use any external cron parsing libraries. The core is a matchesField(value, n, min) function that handles all the special cron characters: *, */n, n-m, n,m, and n/m. The next-run calculator works by starting from the current minute and incrementing forward, checking each minute against all 5 fields until it finds 5 matches. It caps at 500,000 iterations to handle edge cases like rare monthly schedules. React + Vite (frontend) Netlify Functions (serverless API) Zero dependencies for the parser IBM Plex Mono font because it felt right for a dev tool I'm thinking about adding: Cron job monitoring (ping a URL, alert if it hasn't run) Reverse builder (describe a schedule in English, get the cron) More languages in the API docs The code is open source on GitHub. Would love feedback, especially on cron expressions that break the parser — there are definitely edge cases I haven't covered. 🔗 Live tool: https://timely-flan-0ca3c1.netlify.app API docs: https://timely-flan-0ca3c1.netlify.app/docs
